instructions: The passage has seven paragraphs, A-G. Choose the correct heading for paragraphs B-G from the list of headings below. There are more headings than paragraphs, so you will not use them all. Paragraph A has been done for you as an example: its heading is 'Why a familiar material deserves a closer look'.

options: Why early builders distrusted lime mortar
How knowledge of the recipe was lost
Competition from steel frames and glass
Steel overcomes a basic weakness
A patented process allows mass production
Harbour structures that outlasted their builders
A volcanic ingredient behind Roman durability
Modern attempts to reduce harm and repair cracks
An engineer's experiments revive interest
items.answer: A volcanic ingredient behind Roman durability

evidence.quote: lime with volcanic ash from the Bay of Naples

items.how: Read paragraph B's opening and middle sentences to find what the Romans added to their mixture, then choose the heading that names that main idea rather than a single example.
items.again: Test the heading about harbour structures: harbours appear only as one illustration of how long the mixture kept reacting. The trap is that a vivid supporting example can look like the topic, when the paragraph is mainly about what the mixture contained and why it worked.

evidence.quote: the knowledge faded as trade networks collapsed

items.how: Look for the sentence in paragraph C that explains what happened after the Roman Empire ended, then check that your heading covers the explanation given for it as well.
items.again: Test the heading about distrust of lime mortar: the paragraph says builders relied on mortar, not that they distrusted it. The trap is that the same material is mentioned, but the writer never describes an attitude towards it.

evidence.quote: patented a method of heating ground limestone and clay

items.how: Find the year and the legal term in paragraph E, then check what the new process allowed builders to do that they could not do before.
items.again: Test the steel-frame heading, which sounds modern and industrial. The trap is that it relates to a different period; the paragraph concerns a powder made from limestone and clay, and says nothing about competing structural materials.
